pharm: Beta-adrenergic agonist (also known as nylidrin) producing peripheral vasodilation, positive inotropy and chronotropy; historically used for peripheral and cerebral vascular disorders.
quick: 3-12 mg orally 3-4 times daily (up to ~90 mg/day)
May be taken with or without food
Avoid unless clearly needed; limited data
Caution; may add to hypotensive/dizziness effects
summary: Buphenine (nylidrin) is a beta-adrenergic agonist that causes peripheral vasodilation with positive inotropic and chronotropic effects, historically used for peripheral vascular disorders (Raynaud's disease, arteriosclerosis obliterans, thromboangiitis obliterans) and cerebrovascular insufficiency. Typical oral dose is 3-12 mg three to four times daily. It has been withdrawn from the US market but may still be available in some countries; this record reflects historical labeling and SmPC/BNF-type sources.
indications: Peripheral vascular disorders (arteriosclerosis obliterans, thromboangiitis obliterans, Raynaud's disease, frostbite sequelae, ischemic ulcers, thrombophlebitis - historical)
Cerebrovascular insufficiency / circulatory disorders of the inner ear (historical)
Adjunct to improve walking distance/healing of trophic ulcers in peripheral arterial disease (historical)

dosage.n: Maximum about 90 mg/day; titrate to response and tolerance

admin: Take orally, with or without food, in divided doses three to four times daily
Titrate dose to symptomatic response and cardiovascular tolerance
Avoid abrupt position changes; rise slowly to reduce dizziness
Discontinue if significant tachycardia, palpitations, or chest discomfort occur
Use under medical supervision given cardiovascular effects
moa: Acts predominantly by beta-adrenergic receptor stimulation, producing peripheral (skeletal muscle) vasodilation, a positive inotropic and chronotropic cardiac effect, and increased blood flow to ischemic tissues, usually with minimal change in overall blood pressure.

absolute: Acute myocardial infarction or recent MI
Severe/unstable coronary artery disease or angina

preg: Avoid unless clearly needed; safety in pregnancy not established.
lact: Avoid during breastfeeding; data on excretion in milk are lacking.
renal: No established dose adjustment; limited data. Use cautiously in significant impairment.
hepatic: Use with caution; limited data on hepatic handling.

moderate: MAO inhibitors and tricyclic antidepressants (potentiated cardiovascular effects)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food
interactions.alcohol: Caution; may add to hypotensive effects and dizziness

monitoring: Symptomatic response (walking distance, ulcer healing, symptom relief)
counsel: Rise slowly from sitting or lying to reduce dizziness
Report palpitations, fast heartbeat, chest pain, or marked dizziness
Tell your doctor if you have heart disease, an overactive thyroid, or take heart/blood-pressure medicines
This is an older medicine withdrawn in some countries; use only as prescribed
pk: Approximately 30 minutes to a few hours
Several hours; supports 3-4 times daily dosing
Store at room temperature, protected from light per label
pearls: NOTE: Buphenine = nylidrin (Arlidin); withdrawn from the US market - this record reflects historical labeling and SmPC/BNF-type sources
Beta-adrenergic agonist - vasodilation accompanied by cardiac stimulation (tachycardia, palpitations)
Efficacy of vasodilators in peripheral vascular disease is now considered limited; largely superseded
Contraindicated in recent MI, tachyarrhythmias, and thyrotoxicosis
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; do not double up. Resume the regular schedule.
overdose: Overdose causes excessive beta-adrenergic effects: marked tachycardia, palpitations, arrhythmias, tremor, hypotension, nausea, and weakness. Manage supportively; a cautious cardioselective beta-blocker may be considered for severe tachyarrhythmia. Monitor cardiac rhythm and blood pressure.
